Volume 18 · Chapter 12

Institutional leadership portfolio and final integration

Professional Author-reviewed · Prerequisites: v18-c11

By the endDefend an integrated strategy and demonstrate the limits and strengths of one's preparation.

Volume 18 · Chapter 12

Institutional leadership portfolio and final integration

Capability. Defend a strategy whose research, teaching, people, governance and financial commitments fit together, and identify exactly which capabilities your own evidence does and does not establish. Prerequisite: real responsibility and leadership evaluation; also use the research and teaching portfolios. Every institution, record, judgment and outcome below is an original fictional teaching specimen. None is evidence that the reader has conducted research, taught people, exercised authority or received external evaluation.

1. Integration means making commitments jointly feasible

A leader can produce five plausible documents that collectively promise impossible work. The strategy allocates staff to research; the teaching plan allocates the same hours again; the budget spends a restricted grant on general operations; the risk memo treats expected receipts as available cash; the portfolio calls all of this delivered. An integrated dossier exposes these collisions before they become commitments. Its unit of analysis is a decision with accountable owners, not a collection of flattering adjectives.

A dossier is an indexed argument with its underlying records. An evidence ceiling is the strongest claim those records support. A constraint rules out an action under a stated authority or model; an objective ranks the remaining actions. A contingent policy specifies actions after each possible observation. A capital floor here is an invented minimum book-equity amount, distinct from cash and from any jurisdiction's regulatory capital rules. A restricted fund can finance only its documented eligible use. A positive total balance need not imply adequate unrestricted cash.

Use a common decision date, units, perimeter and version across the strategy, resource ledger, research design, teaching plan and risk appendix. Distinguish a planning production function from estimated performance, and distinguish an estimated association from an identified effect. Carry one assumption register through every artifact. If the research design changes, update its resource requirements and the teaching materials that explain it. If a risk limit changes, recompute the feasible strategy before preserving an old recommendation.

The inspected HBS General Management Program overview connects enterprise strategy, financial management, accounting and multidisciplinary leadership, and names a strategy statement, action plan and business case among its features. The inspected HBS Business Economics requirements connect case discussion with research opportunities and include an advised research paper. These are narrow curricular comparisons, checked 17 October 2026. Our models, portfolio gates and evaluation protocol are original; they confer no institutional credential or endorsement.

2. Two tools for defending an integrated decision

Balanced attainment. When two mission outputs have distinct units, compare each with an explicit target before taking their minimum. For research index R, teaching index T and positive targets R₀,T₀, let z=min(R/R₀,T/T₀). Maximizing z improves the less well-served mission; it does not assert that a research index and a learning outcome are interchangeable. The targets embody a value judgment that a governing body must defend. An arithmetic average would allow one mission to compensate for abandoning the other.

Suppose R=α√x and T=β√y for nonnegative divisible effort x,y, with α,β and targets positive. Set a=(R₀/α)² and b=(T₀/β)². Attaining z requires x≥az²,y≥bz². If effort costs one currency unit per unit, total staff capacity is H, research-only grant is g, and unrestricted spending capacity after fixed obligations and reserve is B, feasibility is x+y≤H and max(x−g,0)+y≤B. The latter uses the grant on research first, as permitted by this model; it is not a general accounting or grant rule.

Write u=z². For H,B,g≥0, every feasible plan satisfies (a+b)u≤H, bu≤B and (a+b)u≤B+g. Conversely, if all three hold, x=au,y=bu is feasible: max(au−g,0)+bu is the larger of bu and (a+b)u−g, both at most B. Thus the global optimum is u*=min{H/(a+b), B/b, (B+g)/(a+b)}. This is an upper bound with an attaining construction, not merely a stationary point. Among all plans attaining z*, choosing the least total effort uniquely selects x=au*,y=bu*: either larger component strictly increases their sum. Without this secondary rule, primary optima can be multiple. When H or B is zero, u*=0; the least-effort plan is zero. If B is negative, even fixed commitments and reserve cannot be financed: report infeasibility rather than a negative square root. Zero targets or production coefficients require a different problem and are excluded here.

Information subject to resource gates. A signal changes the conditional probability of a state. Bayes' rule follows by dividing the joint probability of that state and signal by the signal's total probability; conditioning on a zero-probability signal is undefined. A posterior below one normally leaves an adverse state possible. If a policy must respect a floor in every state in its stated support, check each supported branch, including intermediate cash balances, before maximizing expected value. An expected balance above a floor is not that check.

For finitely many signal branches, with no resource coupling between mutually exclusive branches, choose the best feasible action separately in each branch. Multiplying each branch's action value by its nonnegative probability and summing proves global optimality: replacing any branch maximum cannot improve the sum. Randomizing among actions gives a convex combination and cannot exceed the largest branch value. Add the diagnostic cost and compare with feasible policies that skip it. Free information can be ignored only if the available actions and constraints stay unchanged; a fee may reduce capital and change the menu. These tools are taught in policy evaluation and decision and are reconstructed here to make the dossier auditable.

3. Two complete synthetic dossiers

A. Alder Institute: fund both missions without spending the reserve twice

A0 — mandate and resource release. At the start of a proposed one-term methods institute, the fictional council permits the director to allocate divisible staff blocks between research preparation and teaching preparation. It requires equal proportional attention to targets R₀=4 and T₀=3, then the least total effort among ties. One block is ten staff hours and costs 1 kCU; the 13 available blocks are 130 hours already agreed with staff. No unpaid overtime is assumed. Forecast indices are R=2√x and T=√y. They measure the toy plan's preparation capacity, not numbers of publishable papers, observed learning or actual research quality.

The institute holds 24 kCU unrestricted cash and 6 kCU received grant cash restricted to research preparation. Fixed essential commitments cost 5 kCU from unrestricted cash. Under a zero-new-receipts stress scenario, unrestricted closing cash must be at least 10. Grant balances cannot count toward this floor. No borrowing, future donation, transfer from another program or additional grant use is authorized. Inputs(unrestricted,restricted,fixed,floor,staff blocks,α,β,R₀,T₀) are (24,6,5,10,13,2,1,4,3).

A1 — completed strategy and allocation proof. “Prepare a modest joint research/teaching program that remains funded if no new receipts arrive. Do not maximize the research index while leaving the teaching commitment unsupported. Retain the two target ratios and the grant restriction in the council decision.” Here B=24−5−10=9,a=4,b=9. The three upper bounds on u are 1,1,15/13, so u*=1,z*=1,x=4,y=9. This uses all 13 blocks. Any primary optimum needs x≥4 and y≥9, so the staff constraint itself makes this baseline allocation unique. Results(B,a,b,u,x,y,R,T) are (9,4,9,1,4,9,4,3). Promising both indices at 110% of target would require at least 13(1.1)²=15.73 blocks, exceeding available staff; an enthusiastic memo does not change that inequality.

A2 — complete cash reconciliation, kCU; all project spending is expensed in this toy cash budget
FundOpeningFixedResearchTeachingClosing
Unrestricted2450910
Restricted research60402

The remaining 2 restricted kCU are not permission to raise the teaching budget to 11. With those extra teaching blocks unrestricted cash would be 8, and staff use 15 would independently exceed 13. The grant is already received; if instead it were merely promised, remove it from the available ledger before choosing the plan. The finance owner must reconcile the actual fund terms and receipts before a real institution could apply this model.

A3 — complete deliverable and governance schedule, all work proposed
Work and allocationDeliverable, owner and acceptance
Research: 4 blocks, 40 hoursResearch lead: 10 hours inspect two closest actual papers; 10 reconstruct one result with documented execution status; 10 write a question, estimand, competing explanation and access plan; 10 revise after methods review. Council funds preparation, not a claim of original discovery. A qualified methods reader must inspect the actual paper and reconstruction before accepting a research claim.
Teaching: 9 blocks, 90 hoursTeaching lead: 20 hours write a two-session allocation lesson and prerequisites; 25 prepare original tasks and full keys; 15 rehearse explanations; 15 deliver an authorized demonstration with a human observer; 15 inspect learner work and revise. These are planned hours including delivery, not evidence that delivery occurred. Teaching reviewer checks actual materials and separately records observed delivery.
Authority and financeCouncil approves targets, scope and 13-block ceiling; director schedules staff within it; finance owner certifies restricted uses and cash; independent research and teaching readers can require correction within their expertise. A donor cannot suppress unfavorable findings or instruct the grader. Conflicts are disclosed and handled through the actual institution's authorized process.

A4 — complete sample lesson and research claim boundary. The demonstration asks: “Why can total closing cash 12 coexist with only 10 usable for general obligations? Show the two ledgers, then explain whether R=4 proves four discoveries.” The key is the restricted 2 and the definition of R as a stipulated preparation index. A transfer task removes the grant; learners must recompute rather than relabel the reserve. The research question is whether protected preparation time improves later research and teaching performance; this allocation exercise identifies no such effect. A future evaluation needs actual outcomes, assignment/selection analysis and a credible counterfactual. Comparing selected institute participants with nonparticipants without addressing selection does not supply it. Preserve drafts, feedback and independently attempted transfer work; polished instructor keys alone cannot establish student learning.

A5 — mock panel decision and defense. The entire exchange is invented calibration material. Finance assessor: “The two fund accounts reconcile and the no-receipt stress floor holds. Funding is supported within the stated model.” Teaching assessor: “The workload and sample task are inspectable; delivery and learning remain unobserved.” Research assessor: “Preparation is funded; originality and a causal effect are unsupported.” Chair: “Approve this plan conditionally on actual authorization and staffing in a real application; do not certify implementation or all-domain leadership.” Examiner: “Why not use the leftover grant for teaching?” Director: “Its restriction excludes that use, and staff capacity also binds. A valid change would require documented authority and a new joint budget; a higher total balance is insufficient.” Examiner: “Does this prove your target weights are right?” Director: “No. Equal proportional attainment is the council's stated value judgment. I can show its consequences and a changed-target calculation, not derive institutional values from the square root.”

A6 — completed development response. “Keep release A1 and its proof. By the proposed week 2 review, obtain actual task-specific methods feedback on the selected reproduction. Before the demonstration, secure an observer, permitted learner-work handling and a common task/key; if these are absent, label delivery pending. By the proposed week 6 review, compare the first task, observed response and new independent transfer task, then revise the explanation. The director owns scheduling; finance owns reconciliation; the external readers own their judgments. No favorable fictional comment can replace their real records. Defer expansion if access, staff or reserve evidence fails.”

B. Beacon Finance: a useful signal does not erase a capital state

B0 — mandate, balance sheet and evidence status. This fictional financial service firm is not specified as a regulated bank; no local capital rule is inferred. Opening cash is 30, other assets 170, liabilities 180 and book equity 20, all in kCU. A required research/training preparation package costs 3 in cash and expense under every policy, leaving cash 27 and equity 17. Other assets and liabilities stay fixed throughout the model. The board's invented limits require cash at least 10 and equity at least 8 after each expense and in every supported terminal state. No new capital or borrowing is available. Inputs(cash,other assets,liabilities,equity,training,cash floor,equity floor) are (30,170,180,20,3,10,8).

The service environment is favorable G or adverse B, with stipulated prior Pr(G)=1/2. These probabilities and gains are planning assumptions, not estimates from actual customers. A single diagnostic costs k=1/2, paid and expensed before a signal. Pr(+|G)=4/5 and Pr(+|B)=1/5. It reports before any rollout; it changes neither the environment nor the action payoffs. Signal parameters(prior,positive likelihood G,positive likelihood B,fee) are (1/2,4/5,1/5,1/2). A signal is diagnostic information, not a randomized treatment assignment or proof that rollout causes the stated gains.

B1 — exhaustive action menu after training; payoff is terminal cash gain/loss after upfront setup
ActionSetup expenseTerminal cash change GTerminal cash change BNet incremental GNet incremental B
H: hold00000
C: capped rollout25-33-5
F: full rollout412-88-12

All terminal gains and losses are cash income or expense in the toy model. There are no taxes, receivables, dividends, asset revaluations or later cash flows. Capped rollout includes a fixed exposure cap; it is not a promise that actual losses could never exceed 3. Real use would require a defensible stress perimeter and execution controls. The objective is expected incremental equity relative to paying the common training cost and holding, subject first to the branch floors.

B2 — full global decision. Without a diagnostic, H has expected increment 0; C has (3−5)/2=−1. F has expectation −2 and, independently, adverse equity 17−12=5 below 8. Only H and C are feasible; H is best. With the diagnostic, joint masses ordered (G+,B+,G−,B−) are (2/5,1/10,1/10,2/5). Both signals have probability 1/2, giving posterior Pr(G|+)=4/5 and Pr(G|−)=1/5. The fee leaves cash 53/2 and equity 33/2 before rollout.

C's conditional incremental value is 3q−5(1−q)=8q−5, so it beats H exactly when q>5/8, with a tie at 5/8. It is feasible after either signal: its worst terminal equity is 33/2−5=23/2 and cash 43/2. F's adverse equity is 33/2−12=9/2, so it is infeasible after either signal because both retain positive adverse probability. On a positive signal, F's conditional value 20q−12=4 exceeds C's 7/5, but its floor violation excludes it. Selecting the larger conditional return first would answer a different question.

The best diagnostic policy is C after + and H after −. Its gross expected increment is (1/2)(7/5)=7/10; after the 1/2 fee it is 1/5, above the no-diagnostic H value 0. Global proof: of the nine pairs from {H,C,F}², five contain F in at least one supported signal branch and fail the capital gate. The remaining policies HH,CH,HC,CC have net values (-1/2,1/5,-11/5,-3/2), respectively, with first letter for +. Every randomized policy is an average of these branch decisions and cannot improve their maximum. This proof depends on the supplied menu and probabilities, not on a claim to have found the best real business strategy.

B3 — complete terminal ledger for the chosen diagnostic policy, kCU; other assets 170 and liabilities 180 in every row

The intermediate minimum for the selected C branch before terminal settlement is cash 49/2 and equity 29/2. The adverse terminal state is worse but still above both floors. Expected closing cash is 136/5 and equity 86/5, exactly 1/5 above the cash 27/equity 17 hold baseline. Expected total assets are 986/5, equal to liabilities 180 plus expected equity. Results(expected cash,equity,assets,minimum terminal cash,equity) are (136/5,86/5,986/5,43/2,23/2). The favorable expectation does not establish a realized benefit; G+ and B+ lead to different outcomes under the same sound conditional choice.

B4 — completed research and teaching package. The common 3 kCU budget assigns 1 to a methods review, 1 to staff instruction and 1 to independent execution-control checking; no double use of these funds is allowed. The research lead must preserve the source population, labeled outcomes, diagnostic version and all classification counts before claiming likelihoods have been estimated. A toy probability table does not substitute for held-out validation or for a causal service-impact study. The methods reviewer will ask whether the intended deployment population differs from the validation population and whether drift changes either likelihood. An actual empirical paper would also need a substantive research question, closest literature, access authority and a defensible identification strategy; this business case alone is not that paper.

The staff lesson presents B1 and asks each analyst to compute the positive posterior and name the forbidden action. The full key is q=4/5, C conditional gain 7/5, F conditional gain 4 but adverse equity 9/2. For transfer, remove diagnostic information and ask why a good-looking realized outcome cannot justify an ex ante full rollout. Independent learner responses must show both a Bayes calculation and a scenario ledger; matching a memorized action letter is insufficient. The instructor retains the prompt, permitted help, first response, feedback and new task. An actual human observer must evaluate delivery; neither the allocated training cash nor this written lesson proves learning.

B5 — completed decision and control memorandum. “Authorize only the stipulated diagnostic/capped-or-hold policy within the fictional case. Treasury verifies the opening balances and books training and diagnostic expenses before releasing a rollout budget. Research owns one authenticated diagnostic version and its assumptions; operations may execute C only after the verified positive signal and an independent control officer confirms the cap and balances. A negative or missing signal means H. Duplicate notifications are not new tests. A changed likelihood, cap, fee or ledger invalidates this release and returns the proposal for review. F remains unauthorized even after +. Finance reconciles actual payments and terminal receipts separately from expectations. If any gate cannot be verified, hold rather than fill the gap with a forecast.”

B6 — mock external judgment and revision. Invented risk examiner: “The branch arithmetic supports this policy under the stipulated state set. It does not establish that the set is exhaustive in an actual institution.” Invented teaching examiner: “The transfer task tests the key conceptual error; no actual student work has been supplied.” Invented research examiner: “The likelihoods are assumptions, so withdraw the phrase ‘validated 80% diagnostic’ from the candidate's first draft.” Candidate's completed response: “Release B2 changes that phrase to ‘stipulated sensitivity 4/5 and false-positive likelihood 1/5’; it retains the earlier draft and recomputes the decision if estimates later change. No likelihood-estimation study or learner evaluation is claimed.” Panel disposition: “Model reasoning supported within scope; actual implementation, empirical calibration, teaching effectiveness and leadership outcomes not yet evaluable.”

4. Move from a model defense to evidence of actual preparation

The chapter teaches decision defense. The separate leadership portfolio cross-assessment requires a learner's own strategy memo, reconciled budget, governance map, hiring/incentive plan, crisis exercise and retrospective on actual responsibility. Solving Alder and Beacon does not complete that submission. Research also requires an actual original paper, inspected works and reproduction/referee artifacts; teaching requires the learner's own materials and actual observed delivery where claimed. Use the complete research dossier and teaching dossier as models while supplying your own work. Reuse one genuine artifact across portfolios only with a clear explanation of the different claims and contribution; do not multiply one observation into several independent evaluations.

Operational evidence register to complete for each real claim
FieldRequired entry
Claim and perimeterOne bounded capability, institution/project, dates and your actual decision authority; identify collaborators and contributions
Record and statusArtifact identifier/version, full underlying record, proposed/authorized/executed/observed status, date and custodian; do not silently promote status
Warrant and competing explanationWhat follows from the record, what remains unidentified, and what evidence could change the judgment
Access and integrityActual permission or documented limitation, conflicts, attribution, redactions and controlled reviewer access; retain enough context for review without disclosing protected records
Evaluation and responseActual named consenting qualified reviewer, relationship/conflicts, precise scope, dated comments, your linked revision and unresolved disagreement

Human evaluation protocol. Before real work, agree on the role, permitted actions, resources, deliverables and observation opportunity with the responsible institution. Freeze a review release after the work. Request a domain expert for the research/strategy argument, a financially competent reader for resource and risk reasoning, and a qualified teaching/people reviewer for observed practice; one person may cover overlapping expertise, with relationships disclosed. Obtain actual agreement rather than inventing signatures. Reviewers inspect the full record and independently write a supported claim, a material weakness, an alternative explanation and a changed-input challenge. A supervisor's evidence of authority is useful but does not become independent just by changing the heading.

Conduct a proposed 45-minute defense: 10 minutes explain the integrated choice, 15 reconstruct one proof/ledger without the prepared answer, 10 respond to a changed resource or evidence assumption, and 10 examine actual implementation and a limitation. Record who attended, questions, permitted aids, responses and remaining issues under the actual recording/access agreement. Reviewer judgments use four states: supported within specified scope; supported with limitations; revision required; not yet evaluable. Apply them separately to governance, economic/research reasoning, finance/risk, teaching/people practice and reflection. A missing observation belongs in the last state, not in a fictional zero-to-100 leadership score. Fabricated evidence, an unreconciled material budget or a false causal claim blocks the affected conclusion until repaired; a strong unrelated artifact cannot average it away.

Complete specimen continuation plan. “My current evidence supports solving the supplied resource and conditional-decision models. It does not yet support an original research contribution, observed instructional effectiveness or successful institutional leadership. In the next authorized project I will take a bounded scheduling/budget responsibility, preserve approvals and actual delivery records, and obtain contemporaneous feedback. I will submit a real reproduction and research question to a qualified methods reader, teach one permitted session with an observer and independent transfer task, and reconcile planned versus actual resources. Proposed review at 30 days checks preparation and authority; at 90 days it checks actual delivery, feedback and revisions. If access or opportunity is absent, those claims remain pending and I narrow the plan. My next assignment should address the largest demonstrated weakness, rather than add another polished version of the same unobserved claim.” These dates are a sample planning cadence, not proof of completed work or a universal career schedule.

5. Exercises

  1. Reconstruct Alder's global bound and all three cash-ledger rows. Show why “spend the leftover 2 on teaching” fails two independent constraints. Distinguish the model's achieved target ratios from actual mission outcomes.
  2. Increase Alder's staff capacity from 13 to 16 blocks, leaving other inputs fixed. Find every primary optimal allocation and the secondary least-effort choice. Explain why more staff alone does not improve the balanced objective.
  3. Separately (a) remove the 6 grant because it was only promised, and (b) retain it but raise the unrestricted floor to 12. In each branch find u*, the least-effort allocation, closing unrestricted/restricted/total cash and unused staff. Write a complete council correction.
  4. Return to baseline Alder, but raise the research target from 4 to 6. Solve for u*,x,y and closing fund balances. State the achieved indices exactly and explain whether this changes the evidence of actual research or teaching.
  5. Reconstruct all Beacon signal probabilities, posteriors, feasible diagnostic policies and values. Audit every terminal ledger row and explain why the positive-signal F return cannot override the floor.
  6. Let Beacon's diagnostic fee be k∈[0,2], leaving its likelihoods and other inputs unchanged. Derive the optimal acquire/skip decision including the tie, prove the feasible action menu on this interval, and compute the chosen policy's worst terminal equity when k=7/10.
  7. Keep the original fee 1/2 but make both signal likelihoods 1/2. Then separately restore original likelihoods and raise the equity floor from 8 to 12. Solve each decision, including any signal policy that becomes infeasible. Give a complete instruction to treasury and the research lead.
  8. A candidate presents A and B as “my successful institute and validated financial rollout,” supplies no real work or human observations, and cites the mock comments as independent approval. Write a full assessment decision and a concrete continuation plan covering all five domains. Include two defense questions with full benchmark answers. Do not fabricate replacement evidence.
Complete solutions and evaluation criteria

1. A global bound and two funds

For u=z², x≥4u,y≥9u imply13u≤13,9u≤9,13u≤15. Thus u≤1, attained at(4,9), with z=1. Equality in staff use makes this primary optimum unique. The unrestricted row is24−5−0−9=10; the restricted row6−4=2; the total30−5−4−9=12. Extra teaching2 would make unrestricted8<10 and staff15>13. It cannot be financed from a research-only fund merely because total cash is positive. The ratios are forecast preparation indices under an invented function; actual papers, observed teaching and effects require their own evidence. Credit proof of attainability and both constraints, not only the answer4,9.

2. Primary optima need not be unique

The bounds are16/13,1,15/13, so u remains1. We need y≥9,x≥4. The unrestricted bound max(x−6,0)+y≤9 forces y=9 and x≤6; staffx+9≤16 does not tighten this interval. Every x∈[4,6],y=9 is a primary optimum. Least total effort selects x4,y9, spending13 and leaving3 staff blocks unused. Results(u,x minimum,x maximum,y,unused at secondary choice) are (1,4,6,9,3). The teaching budget binds proportional attainment; extra research alone raises only the already adequate mission. Credit the whole interval and distinction between primary multiplicity and secondary uniqueness.

3. Changed available funds require a changed plan

(a) With g0, B9, u=min(1,1,9/13)=9/13. The least-effort choice is x36/13,y81/13, costing9 and leaving4 blocks unused. Closing unrestricted is24−5−9=10, restricted0,total10. (b) With floor12, B7, bounds1,7/9,1 give u7/9. Choose x28/9,y7, total91/9; research is fully grant-funded. Closing unrestricted12, restricted6−28/9=26/9,total134/9, unused staff26/9. Results in each branch(u,x,y,unrestricted,restricted,total,unused) are ((9/13,36/13,81/13,10,0,10,4),(7/9,28/9,7,12,26/9,134/9,26/9)).

Council correction: “Replace the earlier available-funds record before committing staff. In branch(a), the grant is not received, so withdraw it and authorize the9-block plan with target ratio3/√13. In branch(b), preserve the received grant's restriction and adopt the higher reserve, choosing91/9 blocks and ratio√7/3. Both are reduced preparation commitments; inform research and teaching leads and revise their schedules explicitly. No revised plan is marked delivered. Finance must verify actual balances before execution.” Credit exact funds and a usable correction rather than an unexplained lower score.

4. A new mission target changes the allocation

Now a9,b9,B9,g6,H13. Bounds13/18,1,5/6 give u13/18, x=y13/2. Research uses6 grant and1/2 unrestricted; teaching uses13/2 unrestricted, totaling7 unrestricted. Closing unrestricted24−5−7=12, restricted0,total12. Achieved R=2√(13/2)=√26 and T=√(13/2), each divided by its new target gives √(13/18). Results(u,x,y,unrestricted,restricted,total) are (13/18,13/2,13/2,12,0,12). Both mission ratios fall below1 because the new target demands more scarce effort; the resulting allocations need real deliberation about priorities. No mathematical change creates an empirical result or an observation of teaching. Credit the changed target coefficient and funding split.

5. Check support before taking an expectation

Joint masses .4,.1,.1,.4 give equal signal masses and posteriors .8,.2. H/C are feasible after either signal; F violates capital in B for both. The four feasible policies HH,CH,HC,CC have fee-inclusive increments−.5,.2,−2.2,−1.5. CH wins and also exceeds skip/H0. For G+, cash30−3−.5−2+5=29.5,equity19.5; B+ replaces+5by−3giving21.5/11.5. Either negative branch holds after expenses at26.5/16.5. Adding170other assets and subtracting180liabilities reconciles every row. Expected cash27.2/equity17.2 exceeds the no-diagnostic hold baseline by.2. F after+ has expected incremental4, but bad-state equity4.5<8; the adverse conditional probability.2 is positive. Full credit requires every ledger, the forbidden branch, and the finite-policy argument rather than comparing only averages.

6. Information has both an economic price and a resource cost

After training and fee, equity17−k and cash27−k. For C the worst terminal equity12−k is at least10 over[0,2], above8; its cash22−k≥20. Its intermediate equity15−k≥13 and cash25−k≥23 also pass. H passes. F's bad equity5−k≤5 fails for every k in the interval. Thus the same feasible menu applies, and CH gross value7/10 is independent of k. Its net value7/10−k is maximal among diagnostic policies because branch ordering is unchanged. Compare skip/H0: acquire if k<7/10, either acquire/CH or skip/H at equality, skip if k>7/10. At equality worst CH equity is12−7/10=113/10, cash213/10. Results(threshold,worst equity,worst cash) are (7/10,113/10,213/10). At k0 the diagnostic is free but does not reveal the state perfectly. Credit feasibility across the entire fee interval and the tie.

7. Information quality and tighter capital are distinct changes

Equal likelihoods leave both posteriors1/2. C has conditional value−1 in either branch, so the best diagnostic policy is HH with net−1/2. Skip and H gives0 and is optimal. With original likelihoods but equity floor12, diagnostic C has bad equity23/2<12 in either branch; F also fails. Only HH is feasible after acquiring, again net−1/2. Without the diagnostic, C's bad equity12 meets the new floor exactly but its expectation−1 loses to H0; F fails. Thus skip/H is again best, for a different reason. Results(posteriors in first change,best diagnostic value,best skip value,C adverse equity without fee,C adverse equity with fee) are (1/2,1/2,-1/2,0,12,23/2).

Instruction: “Treasury must not pay for the proposed diagnostic under either revised release. Maintain the common3 training budget and hold rollout; confirm cash27/equity17. In the uninformative branch, research must explain the loss of discrimination rather than claim a positive label validates C. In the tighter-capital branch, retain the informative likelihoods but withdraw C after any signal, since the fee consumes the adverse-state margin. Preserve both old and new releases and record which premise changed.” Credit the distinction; identical actions do not imply identical reasons.

8. A complete assessment decision

“Decision: revision required for the claim of actual success and independent approval. Governance: these models describe authority but contain no record of your own mandate or action. Economic/research reasoning: correct reconstructions may support model competence; they establish no original finding or diagnostic calibration. Finance/risk: the ledger and gates can be assessed as calculations, not as actual treasury performance. Teaching/people: the lesson is reviewable design, while delivery, staff leadership and learner response are not yet evaluable. Reflection: replace the false success statements, preserve the corrected version and state the limits. The mock panel is fictional and cannot supply independent approval. No favorable score in another domain repairs that misattribution.”

“Continuation: first submit corrected model claims and independent solutions. Then obtain a genuine bounded project role with documented authority, resources and access conditions; do not assume authority from this exercise. Maintain actual approvals, decisions, team contributions, deliveries and budget reconciliation. Arrange qualified research/financial review and an authorized teaching observation; preserve their own written scope, conflicts and comments. At a proposed30-day review inspect preparation and unresolved access; at90days inspect actual outcomes and revise the claim ledger. If the work has not occurred or reviewers have not agreed, retain pending status. A real research paper and the later leadership cross-assessment remain separate substantive requirements.”

Defense question1: “Does another3 staff blocks improve Alder's primary objective?” Benchmark: “No; u remains1 because unrestricted teaching capacity is9. Primary optima have y9,x4to6; least effort selects4,9.” Question2: “Why refuse F after a positive Beacon signal?” Benchmark: “The posterior adverse probability is1/5, so the adverse branch remains supported. Equity9/2 violates8 even though F's conditional increment4 exceeds C's7/5. A changed authorization or funded capital plan would need a new analysis, not a relabeled expectation.” Credit a full five-domain judgment, honest correction, actionable actual-work plan and both complete answers. No invented names, observations or signatures earn credit.

6. Teach-back and delayed retention

Teach-back. In three minutes explain why an optimal allocation is not a completed portfolio, why restricted cash is not general reserve and why a likely favorable state does not cancel a scenario floor. Answer guide: Alder's proof establishes a conditional resource optimum; it says nothing about whether work happened. Its2 restricted remainder cannot support general obligations. Beacon's positive signal retains an adverse branch, so floor checks precede expected-value comparisons. A strong explanation supplies these concrete examples and identifies the real records and human review needed to advance each claim.

Delayed task. After two weeks without the solutions, keep baseline Alder except raise available unrestricted spending B from9 to12 while holding H13,g6. Then keep baseline Beacon but suppose a positive diagnostic is followed by the adverse state. Recompute the academic optimum and financial closing ledger; judge whether the adverse outcome alone proves the ex ante choice wrong. Full guide: Alder's bounds are1,4/3,18/13, so u1,x4,y9 remain uniquely optimal under staff capacity. Additional unrestricted resources alone do not improve the objective; unused authorized spending is3. Beacon's B+ row has cash43/2,other assets170,total383/2,liabilities180,equity23/2. The supported adverse outcome does not alone disprove the prior decision criterion or likelihoods; compare the actual execution with the policy and accumulate suitable calibration evidence. Results(u,x,y,unused spending,cash,equity) are (1,4,9,3,43/2,23/2).

Deeper study and continuing development. The two functions and finite state set omit indivisible hiring, institutional politics, legal duties, tail events, research uncertainty and long-run learning. Actual authority and applicable requirements must be established in the real setting; the invented floors and grants are not legal advice. Revisit the research and teaching portfolios, the volume's full assessment/project work and the separate real-work leadership submission. Preparation advances through new substantive work, independent criticism and corrected decisions over time; completing this chapter cannot certify mastery of every frontier or guarantee an appointment.
